pie: h₂éwsos léwka déywi n̥smé ḱludʰí h₁yéh₂ nókʷtm̥ skélHs h₁yéh₂ sóh₂wl̥ wédʰesi. ḱósyo wiHrósyo h₃kʷbʰós bʰéh₂os dh₃dʰí h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁élḱos mḗde. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos h₂énǵʰos h₂epó bʰéroyh₁t. kréwh₂s h₂sowséye bʰéwdʰtu-kʷe. gʷíh₃woyh₁t téwe-kʷe bʰéh₂os h₂ew kʷḱyéh₁t.
english: Dawn, bright goddess, hear us, you who split the night, you who lead the sun! Give light to the eyes of this man, and heal his sore. May the wheel of the sun carry the sorrow away. Dry the blood, and let him wake up. May he live and see your light again.

pie: nu gʷówes ḱóymom gʷm̥té. poh₂imḗn usmé wédʰeti. nu wih₁rós énu sékʷetor. h₁regʷesyéti mē h₃slidʰté mē-kʷe kʷis n̥ḱyéh₁t. pótnih₂ gʷṓs dʰwóri h₂mélǵti. lewkós h₂éydʰos sédesi dʰégʷʰeti.
english: Now, cattle, come home to the village! The shepherd leads you. Now the man follows along. It is getting dark. Do not slip away, and let no one be lost. At the door the mistress milks the cattle. In the dwelling the bright blaze burns.

pie: h₃rḗǵs ḱéyo mḗdonts-kʷe h₂nḗr h₁épi sédyet. gʷíh₃wōh₂? h₃réǵ gʷíh₃wēsi h₁yód légʰyēsi píph₃ēsi-kʷe. kʷíd tébʰye déh₃oh₂? mē moy kʷim déh₃s. dyubʰós dóh₃r̥ h₁áydʰi. nu h₃rḗǵs h₁ésmey dóh₃r̥ h₁áyt bʰéwdʰt-kʷe.
english: The king lay down, and the healer sat beside him. 'Shall I live?' 'King, you shall live, if you lie down and drink.' 'What shall I give you?' 'Give me nothing. Give Dyeus a gift.' Then the king gave him a gift, and awoke.

pie: nókʷts gʷémt wiḱpótis-kʷe légʰt. bʰór wiḱpóteys dʰwórm̥ mē gʷm̥yés. téwe h₃ókʷih₁ mē widóyh₁tām. nu bʰór téwe dóws ḱr̥mh₂yéh₁t. ḱwṓ bʰéwdʰeti deywós-kʷe ḱóymom péh₂sti. h₁yós gʷṓs stéh₂yeti só mr̥yéh₁t.
english: Night has come, and the master has lain down. Thief, do not come to the master's door! Let your eyes not see. Now, thief, let your arm go slack. The dog is awake, and the god guards the home. Whoever steals the cattle, let him die.

pie: h₂ówis, (H)yésmin h₂wlh₂néh₂ ne éh₁est, dedorḱe (h₁)éḱwons, tóm, wóǵʰom gʷérh₂um wéǵʰontm, tóm, bʰórom méǵoh₂m, tóm, dʰǵʰémonm h₂oHḱú bʰérontm.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: ǵʰoysós h₁mé gʰbʰéli térh₃t. méne h₁ésh₂r̥ h₁éǵʰs h₁éyti. ní ḱéyh₂er h₁regʷesyéti-kʷe. kʷŕ̥meyes méne h₃ésth₁h₂ gʷr̥h₃ṓnti. méne swesréy mluHdʰí ǵʰoysóh₁ séngʷt. mē HréwdHs méne h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁éseti.
english: The spear wounded me in the head. My blood goes out. I lie down, and it is getting dark. The worms will eat my bones. Tell my sister: he fell by the spear. Do not cry out; my name shall be famous.

pie: pérkʷunos wih₁rṓm ḱérdh₂ dedórḱe. h₁yós gʰóstis dʰrugʰyéti só n̥ḱyéh₁t. bʰoydʰéh₂ sth₂éh₁yetu h₁íh₂-kʷe méǵh₂ih₂. h₁yós bʰoydʰéh₂m péh₂sti só gʷíh₃wēti. deywṓs bʰoydʰéh₂s wékʷos ḱluwént. gʰóstim sédos h₁n̥dó wédʰe.
english: Perkunos has seen the hearts of men. Whoever deceives the guest, let him vanish. Let the oath stand; it is great. He who guards the pledge shall live. The gods have heard the word of the oath. Lead the guest into the dwelling.

pie: h₁yód ḱérdi dʰégʷʰeti tód studyéh₁t. wódr̥ h₂nérm̥ swéh₂-kʷe h₃ésth₁h₂ gʷm̥dʰí. nu légʰtu swidyétu-kʷe. péh₂wr̥-ge h₂epó lityéh₁t. nókʷts h₁íd h₂epó bʰérēti. h₂éwsōs léwkt gʷíh₃weti-kʷe.
english: What burns in the heart, let that grow cold! Water, come to the man and to his own bones! Now let him lie down and sweat. May the fire indeed go away. Night shall carry it away. Dawn shines, and he lives.

pie: méne ḱwṓ mr̥tós méne ḱéywos h₁ést. h₁mé lóyseh₂i énu sékʷeto. h₁yód wĺ̥kʷos h₁ért h₁ím úd ǵʰéyt. h₁ésyo h₃ókʷih₁ lewkóyh₁ h₁stā́m. nu Hn̥dʰí h₂én légʰyeti ḱéywe l̥gʰdʰí. nu kʷís kʷsépi bʰéwdʰēti?
english: My dog is dead, he was my dear friend. He followed me along the furrow. When the wolf arrived, he drove it out. His eyes were bright. Now he lies there below, lie down, dear friend. Who shall stay awake now, in the night?

pie: awis, yasmin warnā na ā ast, dadarka akwams, tam, wāgʰam garum wagʰantam, tam, bʰāram magʰam, tam, manum āku bʰarantam.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: h₁éḱwōs h₂éǵroy ḱéyro ne-kʷe stesth₂ḗr. pótnih₂ h₁épi sédyet péh₂wr̥-kʷe dʰégʷʰet. nu h₂wést. h₁íns spéḱyet h₂éǵt-kʷe. sth₂té mē-kʷe bʰih₂té. nu sth₂ént pró-kʷe gʷh₂ént.
english: The horses lay in the field and were not standing. The mistress sat beside them, and the fire burned. Then it dawned. She looked at them and said: 'Stand up, and do not be afraid!' Then they stood up and went forth.

pie: dyéw ph₂ter dʰoHnéh₂i h₂wr̥syéh₁t. dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter h₁íh₂m̥ bʰére. gʷṓs yugté lóyseh₂m-kʷe h₂érh₃yōmes. dʰoHnéh₂ lóyseh₂i h₃pusyéh₁t. sóh₂wl̥ h₁íh₂m̥ pékʷoyh₁t. h₂óweyes sph₁réh₂es h₁sih₁ént. h₃épos r̥h₁dʰyéh₁t yugóm-kʷe mē Hrumpih₁tó.
english: Father Dyeus, let it rain on the grain! Mother Earth, bear it. Yoke the cattle, and let us plough the furrow. May the grain increase in the furrow. May the sun ripen it. May the sheep be fat. May the work succeed, and may the yoke not break.

pie: gʰósteyes h₁rént h₂éydʰos-kʷe ḱóymom gʷr̥h₃ét. nu Hrowpóm h₁éǵʰs bʰoréyont. méne bʰréh₂teres kúdʰe h₁sénti? méne swésores kúdʰe h₁sénti? nu kʷís ḱóymom démēti? pérkʷune ḱód dedórḱth₂e?
english: The enemies arrived, and a blaze devoured the village. Then they carried off the plunder. Where are my brothers? Where are my sisters? Now who shall build the village? Perkunos, do you see this?

pie: dʰéǵʰom méne bʰréh₂term̥ h₁áyso h₁ím h₂lékse. bʰréh₂ter pr̥kʷéwi Hn̥dʰí l̥gʰdʰí. pr̥kʷéws wréh₂des téwe h₃ésth₁h₂ térdonti. péruti h₂uksté nu Hn̥dʰí légʰyesi. pérkʷunos téwe h₁nómn̥ widyéh₁t. téwe h₁nómn̥ mē n̥ḱyéh₁t.
english: Earth, receive my brother, protect him. Lie down, brother, under the oak. The roots of the oak shall bore through your bones. Last year you grew tall, now you lie below. May Perkunos know your name. May your name not vanish.

pie: h₂wést h₂éǵrom gʷā́m pr̥kʷéws-kʷe wréh₂dm̥ h₂isḱóm. h₁íh₂m̥ widóm h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe úd dérom. h₁íh₂m̥ wédni dʰédʰeh₁m̥ h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe gʷʰr̥nḗm. gʰostéyey h₁íh₂m̥ h₁ā́m péh₃t-kʷe. dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr méǵʰye wréh₂dm̥ h₁áyt h₁ím-kʷe spért.
english: It dawned. I went to the field and sought the oak's root. I found it and tore it up. I put it into water and heated it. I gave it to the guest, and he drank. Mother Earth gave me the root, and she has rescued him.

pie: sérpont h₂éngʷʰey lóyseh₂i l̥gʰdʰí. h₂ówins mē h₁r̥sḱés poh₂iménm̥ mē h₁r̥sḱés. nu ḱwṓ bʰéwdʰeti twé kʷéḱt. h₂epó sérpe nu bʰudʰménm̥ ní h₁idʰí. wih₁rós kʷis ǵʰwḗr-kʷe mē n̥ḱyéh₁t.
english: Snake, creeping in the furrow, lie down! Do not go to the sheep, do not go to the shepherd. Now the dog is awake, he sees you. Creep away, now go down to the bottom. May no one be lost, man and beast alike.

pie: bʰréh₂tēr mr̥yéto h₁ésyo-kʷe swésōr h₁épi sédyet. h₂énǵʰos h₁íh₂m̥ gʷr̥h₃ét. h₂éǵt. déywe méne bʰréh₂term̥ mē h₁éps. gʷíh₃woyh₁t. nókʷts léytt. bʰéh₂os h₂usési widét swesrés-kʷe ḱḗr méwdt.
english: The brother was dying, and his sister sat beside him. Grief ate her. She spoke: 'God, do not seize my brother! May he live!' The night went by. At dawn he saw the light, and his sister's heart rejoiced.

pie: h₃rḗǵs mért h₁ésyo ḱléwos méǵh₂. nu h₁ésyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti. h₁ésyo wéyHs méǵh₂ih₂ h₁ést. wiḱpóteyes stesth₂ḗr HrudHénti-kʷe. Hróth₂os stestóh₂e h₂eǵós-kʷe ne h₁ésti. ḱlutóm h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t.
english: The king has died, his fame is great. Now his fame shall be imperishable. His strength was great. The lords stand and cry out. The chariot is standing, and there is no driver. May his famous name be great.

pie: ne h₂wérst lóyseh₂ térst dʰoHnéh₂ ne bʰwéh₂t. ǵʰwḗres tr̥syónti tr̥syómes-kʷe. upó spéḱyomes n̥smé mē linékʷs. pérkʷune ne h₂wérseti? ḱm̥h₂mé wéyHs-kʷe nos lelóykʷe.
english: It has not rained, the furrow has dried up, the grain does not grow. The wild beasts are thirsty, and we are thirsty. We look up, do not leave us. Perkunos, will it not rain? We have grown tired, and our strength is gone.

pie: h₂éḱruh₂ méne h₃kʷsú h₁ésti. méne suHnús lelóykʷe. wĺ̥kʷos h₁ím ne h₁épt ǵʰoysós-kʷe h₁ím ne térh₃t. h₁ím kʷis sléh₂gʷt h₁ím-kʷe wéydsoh₂. h₂énǵʰos méne gudóm gʷr̥h₃éti. kʷís méǵʰye h₁ím h₁opéyēti?
english: Tears are in my eyes. My son is gone. The wolf did not seize him, and the spear did not wound him. Someone has seized him, and I long to see him. Grief eats my entrails. Who will give him to me?

pie: péh₂wr̥ wórmons h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂i h₁éwse. kʷŕ̥mins h₁éwse h₂ōwyéh₂ h₁éwse. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m mē h₁éwses sédos mē h₁éwses. h₂éwis h₂wĺ̥h₁na lewkéh₂ bʰuHdʰí. nu wih₁rós h₁íh₂m̥ m̥dʰúh₁ h₂linéHti. wórmōs h₁ésmi méronti.
english: Fire, burn the grubs in the wool! Burn the worms, burn the eggs. Do not burn the wool, do not burn the dwelling. Be bright, wool of the sheep. Now the man smears it with honey. The grubs shall die in it.

pie: bʰéh₂os sn̥gʷtā́m h₂ew-kʷe h₁ludʰét. dʰoHnéh₂ ní séngʷt h₂wékst-kʷe. h₁yód nos bʰéh₂os séngʷeti h₂ew ne gʷm̥sḱómes. ǵn̥h₁yómesdʰh₂ mr̥yómesdʰh₂-kʷe. ḱléwos ne mért ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos h₁ésti.
english: The light goes down and comes again. The grain sinks down and grows. When our light has set, we do not come again. We are born, and we die. Fame does not die, imperishable fame remains.

pie: nu dyéw ph₂ter h₂wr̥syéh₁t h₂wr̥syéh₁t. pérkʷunos pérkʷum stunddʰí. nu wódr̥ diwés ní h₁ludʰét. dʰéǵʰōm tr̥syéti péh₃tu pléh₁tu-kʷe. dʰoHnéh₂ h₂wékseti ḱód dóh₃r̥ méǵh₂.
english: Now, Father Dyeus, may it rain, may it rain! Perkunos, strike the oak. Now the water comes down from the sky. The earth is thirsty; let her drink and be full. Then the grain will grow, great is this gift.

pie: h₁éḱwos h₂éǵroy ḱéyo ne-kʷe h₁ḗdt. wiHrós h₁ím widét h₃ésth₁ Hrumptó. h₃ésth₁ h₃roǵéyet h₁íd-kʷe ḱélet. dʰoHnéh₂m bʰéret h₁ésmey-kʷe h₁íh₂m̥ dédeh₃t. nu h₁éḱwos sth₂éh₁yet h₁ḗdt-kʷe.
english: The horse lay in the field and did not eat. The man saw it: the bone was broken. He straightened the bone and covered it. He brought grain and gave it to the horse. Then the horse stood and ate.

pie: kréwh₂s sth₂éh₁ye h₁éǵʰs-kʷe mē léyts. sh₂imónm̥ h₁élḱesi péri logʰéyoh₂. sh₂wéns h₃ókʷ h₁íd spéḱyoyh₁t. sóh₂wl̥ kréwh₂s h₂sowséyoyh₁t. dʰwṓr Hwr̥tó h₁ésh₂r̥ h₁n̥dóm sédyeti. tébʰye wékʷos trís wéwkom.
english: Blood, stand still, and do not go out! I lay a cord around the sore. May the eye of the sun look upon it. May the sun dry the blood. The door is shut, the blood stays within. Thrice I speak the word to you.

pie: méne wiHrós pr̥kʷéwi Hn̥dʰí ḱéyor. h₁ésyo kʷis sédesi ne sísdeti. h₂énǵʰesos wéstrom wésh₂er. nu kʷís yugóm yéwgeti? kʷís méne lóyseh₂m h₂érh₃yēti? méne sédos h₂ew wiḱdʰí. mr̥tṓs-ge ne ḱl̥nwénti. h₁wésu téwe ḱléwos h₂uksyéh₁t.
english: My husband lies under the oak. No one sits down in his seat. I wear the garment of grief. Now who shall harness the yoke? Who shall plough my furrow? Come back into my home. The dead indeed do not listen. May your good fame grow.

pie: tod ḱeḱruwos owis aǵrom ebʰuget.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: h₁yód kʷesyo h₃ésth₁ Hrunépetor dóws h₃roǵéye. h₁íd h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ ḱéle sh₂imónm̥-kʷe péri logʰéye. h₁ésmey médʰu h₁opéye píph₃etu-kʷe. mē sth₂éh₁yet légʰyetu. h₁yód h₁néwn̥ nókʷtes léytonti stéh₂tu. h₁yód h₃ésth₁ ne Hwérdʰeti mē bʰéyh₂s. tóm h₂isḱé h₁yós wóyde.
english: When someone's bone breaks, straighten the arm. Cover it with wool and lay a cord around it. Give him mead, and let him drink. Let him not stand up, but let him lie down. When nine nights have gone, let him rise. If the bone does not grow strong, do not be afraid: seek the one who knows.
